intended_object: The circuit size complexity of a Boolean function f : {0,1}^N → {0,1} over a functionally complete basis B: the smallest size of a single-output circuit over B that computes f. Inferred from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
The definition takes `Nat.find` of the set `realizationSizes B f`, which is the set of sizes `c.size` of all circuits `c : Circuit B N 1 G` whose single output equals `f`. `Nat.find` returns the least element of that set. The set is nonempty because the basis is complete: `CompleteBasis` gives a circuit for the one-output function x ↦ (fun _ => f x). The private lemma `sizeComplexity_eq_sInf` confirms the value is `sInf (realizationSizes B f)`. So the definition is the minimum circuit size, as intended.

Size follows the library's stated convention, `G + M` (internal gates plus output gates). Input vertices are not counted and negations on inputs are free. The `size` docstring says this openly and notes that other texts' conventions agree only up to additive or linear overhead. This is a standard variant convention, not an error.

The `NeZero N` hypothesis comes from the library's `Circuit` structure, so it is part of the framework, not a flaw in this definition. The general case of possibly incomplete bases is covered by the companion `sizeComplexityWithTop`, which takes values in `WithTop ℕ`.

Mathlib has no Boolean circuit complexity, so there is nothing more general to compare with.
